start.content: I am a merchant from Tyre. I trade in spices and stories — both travel well along the Roman roads. I heard the Galilean tell the story of the vineyard in the Temple courtyard.

vineyard.content: There was a man who planted a vineyard. He put a fence around it, dug a winepress, and built a watchtower. Then he leased it to tenants and went away. At harvest, he sent servants to collect his fruit. The tenants beat one, killed another, stoned a third.

reaction.content: The crowd murmured. They knew the story. It was Isaiah 5, sung in the synagogues every year. But this time, the tenants were standing in the front row — and the teller was looking right at them.

closing.content: The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. That is how the story ended. The chief priests left early. They did not want to hear the rest.
